caseno: Death Reference No. 21 of 1994 with Jail Appeal No. 2321 of 1994.
lawyer:
Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate — For the Condemned Prisoner. 
MA Rouf, Assistant Attorney-General — For the State.
parties:
State ------ Petitioner-Other Party
vs
Hasen Ali ------ Condemned Prisoner
full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed J: This Death Reference has been made by the Sessions Judge, Kurigram on the basis of his impugned judgment and order passed on 31-10-94 in Sessions Trial case No. 38 of 1993. Jail Appeal 2321 of 1994 also was preferred by the convict condemned prisoner Hasen Ali which is also taken up for hearing and disposed of by this one judgment. Two other accused namely, Ahadullah and Alam @ Kurshed Alam, were tried in the same case, but they were acquitted. 

 2. The case for the prosecution, in short, is that, the PW 1 Zahura Khatun, wife of the deceased Abdul Kashem, lodged the First Information Report (Exhibit 1) in the local Razipur Police Station on 11-5-93 at 06-30 hours of the said date alleging that the deceased Abdul Kashem who was a dealer in cattle, was returning home at 08-45 hours at night on 10-5-93 from the local Kodalkati hat along with his cousin brother Habibur Rahman, PW 8 and accused Ahadullah who has been acquitted and when they reached by the side of Badarpur Madrasha and primary school a person came out from the nearby Kalmi bush and stabbed the deceased and fled away towards south. The victim then fell down and died there. PW 8 Habibur Rahman then chased the said person who stabbed the victim because the man was running the bed sheet by which the man covered his face fell down and then Habibur Rahman, PW 8 could recognise that it was Hasan the condemned prisoner. It is to be noted that Hasan and the PW 8 Habibur Rahman are full brothers. Three brothers used to reside in the same house. He narrated the story as to the occurrence to the informant, the wife of the deceased, and on the next morning, she lodged the First Information Report. In the First Information Report it is stated কে বা কাহারা ডেগার দ্বারা হত্যা করিয়াছে 

 The police came, held inquest and seized alamats, the knife and bed sheet, etc. and post mortem was held upon the dead body by the PW 14 Dr Md A Rashid. After the investigation, the police submitted charge sheet under sections 302/109 of the Penal Code against the three accused Hasan Ali, the condemned prisoner, said Ahadullah and Khurshed Alam. Further prosecution case is that, after the incident Hasan absconded from the locality for about one month and then came back, local Chowkider then arrested him and handed him over to the police. 

 4. In this case, the PW 8 Md Habibur Rahman is the only eye-witness. He narrated the story of the occurrence at the time of trial. He stated that his brother the deceased was also a cattle dealer. His testified that when himself along with one Ahadullah started for home and when reached Badarpur Hafizia Madrasha at about 8-00 PM a man covering his face by cloth came out from the road side Kalmi bush and stabbed Kashem with a knife on his belly. Kashem fell down on the ground raising alarm. He (PW 8) also raised alarm and chased the man who stabbed the deceased, the cloth of the man by which he covered his face fell down and he then could recognize that the man was Hasan the condemned prisoner. In his cross examination, this PW 8 stated that the night of occurrence was dark. He further stated that the man was covered by a bed sheet from his head to foot. He also stated that he did not see the knife. The knife was not produced before the Court. In the First Information Report, wife of the deceased stated that the PW 8 after returning home narrated the story about killing of her husband to her and other inmates of the house including a son of the deceased named Asanuddin. She also admitted that she had talks over the incident with Habibur Rahman. The local people assembled in the place of occurrence and suspected Hasan and also Alam (Khurshed Alam) co-accused of Hasan to have killed her husband because there was a land dispute between her husband and Hasan. The accused Alam is a friend of Hasan. She named Hasan and Khurshed Alam while deposing at trial as assailants and the local people suspected them. 

 5. PW 2 Md Rafiqul Islam who is the local Chairman. He stated that on the next morning when he was returning to his house at about 8-00 AM from Razibpur UP office on the way, he came to know that a cattle dealer was killed on the road to the east of the Badarpur Madrasha and he went there and found the dead body being surrounded by the local people. He found a knife by the side of the dead body but PW 8 the only eye-witness in the case did not see the knife and he stated that one man came out from the Kalmi bush and stabbed the victim and he fled away. In his cross examination he stated that he deposed against accused Khorshed Alam in a theft case but he was acquitted. PW 3 Md Amiruddin Miah is the former Chairman of the local Union Parishad. He also went to the place of occurrence immediately after killing and found the dead body of Kashem lying. He also found an injury on the left side of the abdomen but he was found dead. He has also deposed that he also heard from the local person present there that someone came out from the bush and stabbed him. This witness stated that on the next morning, the informant went to the police station with him and the chairman, PW 2 and lodged the First Information Report and they suspected accused Hasan to be involved in. the occurrence. This witness admitted in cross that he did not state to the investigating officer that he heard from Habibur Rahman (PW 8) that Hasan assaulted Kashem. PW 4 Manullal Skeikh, he simply stated that he saw Hasan on the next morning to leave his village since people suspected that Abul Kashem was killed by Hasan. In cross-examination, this witness stated that Hasan did not confess to him that when he was returning from said Kodal Kati market. He stated that he heard hue and cry from the side of Badarpur Primary School and went there and found the dead body of Kashem with bleeding injury. He deposed in chief which is as follows: 

 "I know from PW Habibur and Ahadullah that someone stabbed Kashem coming out from the bush, I did not mark if there was any dagger by the side of dead body. After the occurrence we did not find Hasan in the locality and so the local people suspected Hasan to have been involved in the occurrence. Later on he heard that Hasan killed Kashem." 

 7. PW 7 is also an important witness. In cross-examination, he said that Hasan is the brother-in-law of his wife. This witness stated that on the night of occurrence at about 9-00 PM Hasan went to him and called him out from his hut. On his enquiry as to why Hasan went there. Hasan''s statement as follow: 

 This witness stated that Hasan disclosed to him about killing of Kashem by him. He further stated that he disclosed the fact of admission of Hasan about the occurrence to Majibur, Jinnat Ali, Sabur Ali, Zainul Abedin, Mabiur Hossain who are his neighbours in that night but this witness did not go to the house of Kashem after the occurrence or to the place of occurrence, although he claimed that he is a near relative of the deceased. He visited the place of occurrence on the following day and none of those persons has been examined. He found the dead body. PW 8 said to be the only eye-witness of the occurrence. We have discussed his evidence earlier. PW 9 Badsha Member stated in chief that he heard about the killing of Kashem and he further stated that when Hasan came back to his village after his absconsion, he (this witness) informed the local Lokhan Chowkidar who then arrested Hasan and when he asked Hasan he confessed that he killed Kashem and many other persons were present there at the time of making confession by Hasen. This witness stated that he did not mention name of any person before whom confession was made, and none of them has been examined. PW 10 Md A Gafur also was tendered and cross-examination denied. PW 11 Md Rafizuddin a Member of the neighbouring Union Parishad. He also stated that he heard that Hasen killed Kashem. He further stated that he met Hasen on the way on the road at Shankar Madhabpur in arrested condition by the Chowkidar and on the way Hasen confessed that he killed Kashem. PW 12 Md Anwar Hossain was tendered and not-cross examined. PW 13 Md Matiur Rahman is the investigating officer. He stated that he found the dagger by the side of the dead body. In cross examination he stated that many local people stated to him that Hasen confessed his guilt but he also stated that accused Hasen did not make confession to him admitting his guilt and he had no plan also to produce Hasen for recording his confessional statement. This PW also could not name anybody before whom Hasen admitted his guilt. PW 14 Dr Md A Rashid. He held post mortem examination upon the dead body. 

 8. Trial Court convicted Hasen relying upon the evidence of PW 8 Md Habibur Rahman who is said to be the only eye-witness of the occurrence and the extra judicial confessional statement of the condemned prisoner, but no confessional statement was recorded under section 164 CrPC by any Magistrate and even oral confession has not been proved in verbatim of Hasen, although stated by PW 7 Md Asmotullah, PW 9 Badsha Member and PW 11 Md Rafazuddin Member. So we cannot understand Or know how and in what manner in or what language Hasen made extra judicial confession. So far the evidence of PW 8 is concerned it is very clear from his deposition and also from the statement of PW 1, wife of the deceased who lodged the First Information Report when PW 8 Md Habibur Rahman and the local Chairman PW 2 accompanied her to the police station and so also Rafazuddin PW 11, but in the First Information Report which is not conclusive evidence but it is a substantive evidence and it forms foundation of the case, the name of Hasen has not been mentioned as killer by wife of the deceased in the first information report. She has merely suspected Hasan although, she immediately after killing, heard from PW 8. She stated that one man came out from the Kalmi bush and stabbed the deceased. She suspected Hasen Ali his co-accused Md Khurshed Alam as assailants of her husband. It is also on evidence and came out from the mouth of PW 5 Taher Munshi who stated that the local people suspected Hasen as assailant of the deceased, So, he absconded from the locality. Mere suspicion or absconsion does not prove the prosecution case against any particular accused. We do not find the reason why this PW 8 Md Habibur Rahman, who is the only eye-witness and a near relative of both the condemned prisoner and the deceased did not disclose the name of Hasen before lodging the First Information Report to PW 1 or at the time of lodging of the First Information Report. There is another very material aspect of the case. The place of occurrence is in a rural area and the time was at night. PW 8 is the only eye-witness. He recognised Hasen at the time of occurrence but is said by PW 8 that the night was dark. So his recognition of Hasen was doubtful and hence Hasen was implicated only by suspicion which comes on the face of the evidence both oral and documentary, from the mouth of almost all the witnesses. This PW 8 also stated that he did not see the knife by the side of the dead body after killing but the investigating officer on the next date at about 01-45 PM when he went to the place of occurrence seized the knife lying by the side of the dead body. This also invites some doubt about the deposition of PW 8 about recognition of Hasen. 

 9. In this case, there were other two accused namely, Ahadullah and Khurshed Alam who were tried and had been acquitted. So far the extra judicial confession of the condemned prisoner is concerned it is oral and vague. It was not written. It is also admitted that when Hasen was being taken by the Chowkidar in arrested condition, Hasen admitted that he killed the victim. So, the alleged admission or confession is of no legal importance. 

 11. In the case of State vs Badsha Molla, reported in 1989 BLD, 257 = 41 DLR 11, in para 21 of the said decision, It has been held as follows: 

 "It is well settled in law that an extra-judicial confession by its very nature has been held to be a very weak type of evidence and it has to be scrutinized with great care and caution and then received. Ordinarily it is unsafe to base conviction of an accused on his extra judicial confession alone. The alleged confession has to be proved like any other fact. The value of evidence as to such confession like any other evidence depends upon the veracity of the witnesses to whom it is made. Once the evidence is rejected as not being reliable, the value of evidence of such confession comes practically to nothing. It is also well settled that in a case of extra judicial confession material corroboration by evidence of unimpeachable character is required to connect the accused with the crime." 

 12. In the case of Jahur vs Crown 6 DLR 246, it has been held as follows : "Without independent evidence of corroboration it is not possible to accept the extra judicial confession as true beyond dispute." 

 13. In this case there is no ocular evidence of the occurrence excepting the testimony of PW 8 Md Habibur Rahman who also did not disclose the name of the condemned prisoner to the PW 1 informant, or to anybody after killing or also at the time of lodging the First Information Report. Although it has been stated by some of the witnesses that Hasen made extra judicial confession admitting the killing of the victim. But we do not get what was the confession, in what language and in what manner. So the allegation of making extra judicial confession has become vague and uncertain and without any corroboration and in exact terms of admission. 

 15. Here in this case, as we find from the deposition of PWs 7, 9 and 11 that Hasen confessed his guilt to them but it is not there either in the language of Hasen or in any specific manner. 

 16. From scrutiny and meticulous reading of the statement of PWs, namely, 7, 9 and 11, it cannot be concluded that really Hasen admitted his guilt to them and the truth and voluntariness also cannot be found or attached with the alleged extra judicial confession of Hasen, which is said to be made to different persons and, as such, the same does not come within the concept of extra judicial confession and cannot be relied upon in a case of the present nature and circumstances, whereas, the trial Court has convicted the condemned prisoner, on the basis mainly of the extra judicial confession of the condemned prisoner. 

 17. Another very important aspect of this case is that, the First Information Report, which is the foundation of the proceeding, we find departure from the First Information Report story in the deposition of the witnesses who testified in the trial. In the First Information Report name of Hasen was not mentioned as the killer but subsequently his name has been incorporated. This departure can be termed as an embellishment brought by the prosecution which cannot be accepted in a case of this nature for awarding death sentence. 

 "First Information Report it being the earliest record of a case, it has got much importance. It enables the Court to see what the prosecution case is when it was started and to check up any subsequent embellishment or any departure therefrom as the case proceeds through different stages." 

 19. When the First Information Report was lodged, there was talk and conversation between the informant and PW 8, the only eye-witness, who also accompanied the informant to the police station. When First Information Report was lodged, then the name of Hasen has not been stated clearly as the assailant, there was merely suspicion against him. 

 "Confession Judicial and Extra-judicial. Distinction lies in degree of caution and proof required in case of each extra-judicial confession to be proved true strictly and with utmost care before corroborative circumstantial evidence can be called in aid of support. The distinction between the judicial confession and extra-judicial confession does not lie in whether they are legally sufficient for basing the conviction of the person upon them but in the degree of caution and proof required in the case of each. In the case which depends solely upon extra judicial confession, the confession has to be proved strictly and utmost care has to be exercised for the purpose of accepting it. If it is after a conclusion has been reached that the evidence relating to the extra-judicial confession is true that the corroboratory circumstances would be called in aid to support the evidence of the witnesses."

 In the result, this Death Reference is rejected, the appeal of the condemned prisoner is allowed and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of death dated 31-10-94 passed in Sessions Trial Case No. 38 of 1993 by the Sessions Judge, Kurigram is set aside. The accused condemned prisoner Hasen Ali is not found guilty of the charge levelled against him and he is, thus acquitted. We direct that the condemned prisoner Hasen Ali, son of late Abdul Gani, be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other cases.
